text: Your operations team already stores returned laptops while waiting for a decision about repair or recycling. A repair triage bench would give those returns a defined route before another storage shelf fills up. The proposal uses the existing spare room and assigns the current technician to inspect devices during the scheduled maintenance block. No additional hire is included. Each laptop would receive a record of the fault, the repair estimate and the final disposition. Devices with damaged batteries would remain isolated under the current handling rules. Working machines would enter the loan pool only after the normal security wipe and hardware check. Repairs would require approval from the equipment owner; the bench would not create a separate purchasing budget. At the end of the pilot, the operations lead would compare repaired units, recycled units and technician time against the previous storage process. The point is to make the fate of returned equipment visible before committing to a permanent workshop. Could you approve a pilot in the spare room?
